repairs.programName: Colorado - Home Electrification and Appliance Rebate (HEAR) Program

formulaRepair.formulaText: For an eligible household with a registered contractor and an available regional reservation pathway, rebate equals the lesser of the selected measure cap, the remaining $14,000 household HEAR cap, and the income-tier percentage of eligible project cost. Income below 80% AMI uses 100% of qualified cost; income from 80% to 150% AMI uses 50% of qualified cost; above 150% AMI is not eligible for HEAR.
eligibleCostCategories: qualified home electrification and appliance upgrades listed by Colorado Energy Office
registered-contractor installed eligible equipment
approved existing-home upgrades for verified low- or moderate-income households
ineligibleCostCategories: retroactive projects completed outside the program pathway
DIY projects
projects not installed by a registered contractor
households above the HEAR income limit
projects in regions without remaining funds or reservation access

calculationTraceTemplate: Confirm regional funding and reservation status before presenting a value.
Confirm household income tier: below 80% AMI, 80%-150% AMI, or ineligible.
Select measure_cap_cents from the official Colorado HEAR table.
Compute income_tier_percent as 1.0 for below 80% AMI or 0.5 for 80%-150% AMI.
Compute gross_rebate_cents = round(income_tier_percent * eligible_project_cost_cents).
Return min(remaining_household_hear_cap_cents, measure_cap_cents, gross_rebate_cents) only when contractor and funding gates are satisfied.

formulaRepair.formulaText: SVP new-construction rebates are deterministic by project pathway, but require project-specific inputs, preapproval, and a current program-year funding/rate confirmation. Air-cooled chillers pay $100 per ton for EER 11.1 to below 12.1 and $150 per ton for EER 12.1 or higher. Qualifying packaged or unitary air conditioners and heat pumps pay $50 per ton. formulaRepair.formulaText: For eligible Santee Cooper Solar Business or Solar Home projects, calculate eligible AC watts as DC watts multiplied by weighted inverter efficiency, subject to the 6 kW AC per meter rebate cap and any customer/system eligibility constraints. Base rebate is $0.95 per eligible AC watt, capped at 6,000 AC watts per eligible meter, or $5,700 per meter.
